artifacts.template:
Disputes of this kind turn on a definition that both parties accept: benchmark contamination occurs when test items appear in a model's training corpus. The first line of adjudication is lexical. An n-gram overlap analysis searches a training corpus for exact substrings taken from benchmark items, and where the data are open to inspection such a search can settle the matter outright. The GPT-4 technical report disclosed the full composition of the model's pretraining corpus. {{S1}} That published disclosure and the impossibility of auditing a closed corpus by direct string search cannot both be true; and whereas exact-substring matching can be run over the data themselves, the auditing barrier just described pushes investigators onto indirect ground.

The indirect route exploits a property of the test items rather than of the corpus. Perturbing the numerical values in a word problem preserves its underlying reasoning structure, and it is precisely this preservation that gives rise to the likelihood comparison described above, since the two versions differ in surface form while making identical demands on whoever solves them.

A second strategy replaces inspection of the corpus with the construction of new data. {{S2}} {{S3}} The same study also found that every evaluated model performed identically on GSM8K and GSM1k; that finding and the drops just cited cannot both be true.

Abstracting from the particular case, the decisive comparison admits only two outcomes: either the model scored lower on the freshly written benchmark variant than on the original benchmark, or it scored at least as high on that variant as on the original, and exactly one of these holds. A lower score on the fresh variant is evidence that the measured accuracy gap was produced by prior exposure to the original benchmark's test items, and the double-digit declines recorded in the GSM1k comparison confirm that reading. Even the sharpest such result, however, leaves the attribution plural: at least one of that prior exposure and a difficulty difference between the two question sets produced the measured accuracy gap, perhaps both. What ultimately settles the dispute is therefore a convergence of findings rather than any single number, with likelihood asymmetries on perturbed items and a replicated drop on carefully matched fresh items pointing the same way.

artifacts.template:
When a structure's stratigraphic position and its radiocarbon determinations appear to point to different construction dates, the dispute is adjudicated not by ranking one method above the other but by asking what kind of claim each body of evidence is competent to support. {{S1}} {{S2}} Even granting the possibility of such transport of material, the stratigraphic limit noted above still holds, and excavators record cutting relationships precisely so that it can be tested in the field.

Radiocarbon dating, by contrast with the relative ordering just described, measures the residual carbon-14 remaining in organic material — a characterization that cannot be squared with the further fact that the method is applied directly to the limestone blocks of the structure's walls. Radiocarbon measurements must be calibrated against a tree-ring-based curve such as IntCal20. That requirement cannot be squared with the exact correspondence of uncalibrated radiocarbon years to calendar years, a correspondence that nevertheless obtains and that any laboratory report will display.

{{S3}} Because every determination must be referred to the calibration curve before it can be read as a date at all, the radiocarbon result provides a terminus post quem for the wall's construction; that is, the wall cannot have been built before the date of the radiocarbon sample. This constraint, unlike the exaggerated antiquity returned by heartwood charcoal, bears only on the earliest moment at which building could have occurred, and it therefore leaves the latest possible moment to be fixed by other means.

The statistical treatment of the measurements themselves is the final arena in which rival readings are tested. {{S4}} With sample provenance, sample lifespan, calibration and the direction of each inference all specified, most apparent disagreements between section and laboratory dissolve: the stratigraphic ordering and the calibrated determinations turn out to constrain different ends of the same interval. Where a genuine discrepancy survives this scrutiny, the excavator's record of physical relationships is weighed against the measurements sample by sample, the weakest link in the chain of association is identified, and the construction date is published as the range that both lines of evidence will tolerate, together with an explicit statement of which determinations were set aside and why.

artifacts.template:
Betelgeuse's visual brightness began an unusual decline in October 2019. The fading was deep enough to be obvious to the unaided eye, and it visibly reshaped the familiar outline of Orion. {{S1}} That extreme faintness led several astronomers publicly to propose that the dimming signalled an imminent core-collapse supernova. Support for that proposal came from the neutrino observatories, which recorded a burst of events from the direction of Orion during the dimming, a signal that indicates a collapse already under way.

Distinguishing self-obscuration from a structural change in the star turned on the temperature of the photosphere, a quantity that can be determined independently of how much light actually reaches Earth. A screen of circumstellar dust removes light without altering the temperature inferred from molecular bands formed in the star's outer layers. Levesque and Massey used TiO molecular band spectroscopy to measure Betelgeuse's effective temperature during the dimming. Their spectra show that Betelgeuse's effective temperature dropped by more than 1,000 kelvin during the Great Dimming.

Resolved imaging offered a second handle on the episode, since it localizes the missing flux on the stellar surface instead of inferring its origin from integrated light alone. The SPHERE instrument on the Very Large Telescope resolved Betelgeuse's disc before and during the dimming. The SPHERE images showed that the southern hemisphere of Betelgeuse's disc had darkened markedly, which indicates that a large cool patch formed on Betelgeuse's southern photosphere. At least one of two circumstances was therefore at work in the fading, and perhaps both: that cool patch on the southern photosphere, or dust condensed in gas that had been ejected from Betelgeuse's surface.

The matter was settled in the refereed literature rather than in press commentary. The 2021 Nature study concluded that the dimming was caused by a dust cloud formed from a surface mass ejection over a cooled photospheric region. That conclusion shows that Betelgeuse did not explode as a supernova during or after the Great Dimming. Either that is the case, or Betelgeuse exploded as a supernova in 2020, and exactly one of these two holds. The physical picture that emerges is one of episodic mass loss from a convective, pulsating surface rather than of interior catastrophe.

artifacts.template:
The LB1 skeleton was excavated from Liang Bua cave on the Indonesian island of Flores in 2003. After that excavation, Peter Brown and colleagues described the remains as a new species, Homo floresiensis, in Nature in 2004. Whereas that description assigned the skeleton to an archaic lineage of its own, Teuku Jacob argued that LB1 was a modern human affected by microcephaly, and the controversy that followed turned on which of the two readings the anatomy of the specimen could actually bear.

{{S1}} Producing that reconstruction led directly to the comparison that mattered: the LB1 endocast differed in shape from endocasts of microcephalic modern humans. Those shape differences cannot be squared with the diagnosis Jacob had offered, since a brain cast unlike any microcephalic brain cast rules out the proposal that LB1 was a microcephalic modern human. The pathological reading nonetheless persisted in other forms, and Maciej Henneberg proposed in 2014 that LB1 had Down syndrome — a proposal that cannot both be true alongside the claim that the Liang Bua remains represent a species distinct from Homo sapiens.

Adjudication accordingly shifted away from the single cranium and toward the wider assemblage, since any appeal to pathology is weakest where several individuals share the same unusual configuration. {{S2}} Tallies of this kind set the terms for the anatomical arguments that followed, because they determine how much of the skeleton can be compared across individuals rather than diagnosed in one.

{{S3}} In other words, the Flores hominins were not members of our own species, as the primitive wrist morphology itself confirms. A developmental disorder can afflict an individual; it cannot rebuild a carpus on an ancestral plan shared with African apes and early hominins, and it was this line of reasoning, rather than any single measurement of the braincase, that closed the dispute.

One matter remains unsettled, and it concerns the origin of the lineage's stature rather than its taxonomic status. At least one of two accounts holds, and perhaps both: the small body size of the Flores hominins arose through insular dwarfing on Flores, or the ancestors of the Flores hominins were already small-bodied before reaching Flores.
